title: agentconsole.v1
description: The bridge protocol between the Mac and the phone: JSON text frames over a WebSocket. A request is {id, op, ...}; the answer is {id, ok: true, data} or {id, ok: false, error}; the Mac also pushes {event, ...}. Binary frames (PHN1, IMG1, WEB1) are described in protocol/README.md. Additive only: every object allows extra fields, and a new field is optional.

Id.description: The request id. The phone sends an integer; the Mac echoes whatever it got, so a string works too. A reply without an id answers a frame the Mac could not read.

ErrorCode.description: Why the Mac refused a request.

SessionControl.description: How the Mac can reach a session: its own pty (console), a background job (job), or not at all (viewOnly).

ChatRole.description: Who wrote a chat message. Tool calls of one step arrive as one tools message.

ChatKind.description: A `!` shell command (text is the command, output what it printed) or the notice that the conversation was compacted. Absent for a normal message.

PromptKind.description: A permission (allow or deny) or a question with options.

SubagentState.description: Whether the subagent is still working.

ImageOrigin.description: Where a chat picture came from.

VizKind.description: Which tab of the viz bundle a spec fills.

type.description: The agent type, for example Explore.

depth.description: 1 for a subagent of the session, 2 for one of its subagents.

PromptQuestion.description: One question of an AskUserQuestion prompt.

Prompt.description: A question or permission a hook on the Mac is waiting on.

Takeover.description: Whether the Mac can take a view-only session over. Only on view-only sessions.

stoppable.description: The original is still running but the Mac can stop it (session.takeover with stopOriginal) and resume.

busy.description: The original is mid-turn: stopping it interrupts the turn.

SessionNode.description: Additive: the node a session runs on in a cluster; an older phone ignores it. Absent for the Mac's own sessions.

online.description: False while the node can't be reached; its sessions stay listed.

LastMessage.description: A cheap marker of Claude's newest reply. A new id means a new reply.

text.description: The first lines of the reply.

Limit.description: One limit of the account a session runs on, as a percentage used.

Facts.description: What the chat header shows: the context in use, the model's window and the account's limits.

contextWindow.description: Absent when the window is unknown.

effort.description: The reasoning effort on the session's latest reply ("high", "xhigh"). Absent when the transcript doesn't say; older Macs never send it.

Session.description: One session the Mac knows about.

entrypoint.description: cli, desktop, job, sdk, or the raw entrypoint the session reported.

activity.description: What a working session is doing, for example Editing main.swift.

tool.description: claude, codex or agy. Additive: an older Mac sends none, an older phone ignores it.

Image.description: A picture a chat message refers to. Only this description travels in the chat; the bytes come from chat.image.

ToolStep.description: One tool call inside a tools message.

diff.description: One string per row: "+added", "-removed", " context". Absent when there is no diff.

toolSummary.description: On tools messages: for example Read 2 files, ran 1 shell command.

queued.description: Sent while the agent was working and not yet taken by it.

steps.description: On tools messages: the calls with input, output and diff. Absent when there are none.

output.description: On shell messages: what the command printed.

Command.description: A slash command a session can run.

VizFailure.description: Why a spec could not be built.

FlowCall.description: One tool call in a flow.

FlowTurn.description: One user turn with its calls.

FlowSpec.description: The flow tab: what the session did.

EntityTable.description: A table of the entity diagram.

id.description: Identifier as drawn in the diagram.

EntityLink.description: A relation between tables, in the order of the diagram's lines.

EntitySpec.description: The entity tab: a database schema as a Mermaid ER diagram.

ModelCount.description: How many requests a model served.

VizSpec.description: What the shared viz bundle renders for one tab. Only the field named by kind is filled, unless empty or error says why not.

InboxAction.description: One button an inbox item offers.

id.description: One of allow, allow_once, allow_always, deny, continue, cancel, done, open, and, from a cluster, move_here, move_anyway, take_back, keep, wait_for and continue_here, and, for a question an agent asks, choice_1 to choice_6, one per choice. open is for the Mac only: the phone shows it disabled and the Mac refuses it. move_here, move_anyway, take_back and continue_here change where sessions run, so a phone asks before it answers with one.

primary.description: The main button of the item.

InboxItem.description: One notification the Mac's inbox holds.

kind.description: secret_approval, secret_request, limit_notice, action_failed or notice, and, from a cluster, primary_unreachable (and its confirm item, primary-unreachable:N:confirm), no_primary, primary_back and session_waits, for a question an agent asks, question, and, for an agent's request for the user's yes, consent (its actions are by label: allow and deny where a phone may answer, else deny and open); a phone treats a kind it doesn't know as notice.

expiresMs.description: When an open item stops waiting.

closedMs.description: When the item was answered, expired or withdrawn.

answer.description: The action id that answered it.

blocking.description: True while something waits on this item: an agent, a vault request, a cluster step. Live: a Mac does not keep it across a restart.

waitingSince.description: When the wait began, in ms. Live, like blocking.

waiter.description: What waits: cli, ask, vault or cluster. Live, like blocking.

alertActions.description: What a banner, a notch card or a menu may offer, as action names: allow, deny, change, open, reply, dismiss, open_form or cancel. Mac only; actions is what a phone may press.

note.description: The user's note with the answer, at most 300 characters.

reason.description: Why it failed or was withdrawn, at most 300 characters.

place.description: Where the item came from, for a person to read.

HelloRequest.description: First message on a connection from a paired phone.

PairRequest.description: First message from a phone that is pairing with the one-time code; the Mac shows its approval sheet.

PingRequest.description: Keep-alive; answered with the Mac's clock.

ChatGetRequest.description: One page of a conversation: the newest limit messages, or the ones before or after a message.

before.description: Id of the oldest message the phone has.

after.description: Id of the newest message the phone has.

VizGetRequest.description: The viz specs of a session.

WebSnapshotRequest.description: A JPEG of a localhost page. The Mac answers with JSON, then a binary WEB1 frame.

url.description: An http(s) URL on localhost or 127.0.0.1; absent: the session's own web URL.

SessionMessageRequest.description: Types a message into a session.

key.description: Additive: one value the phone makes up for each command it sends and repeats unchanged on every retry. A Standby that holds or relays the command uses it to tell a retry of the same command from a different command. Without it, the request id, op and arguments stand in. An older Mac ignores it.

SessionSendNowRequest.description: Interrupts the running turn so the queued message runs next.

key.description: Additive: one value the phone makes up for each command it sends and repeats unchanged on every retry. A Standby that holds or relays the command uses it to tell a retry of the same command from a different command. Without it, the request id, op and arguments stand in. An older Mac ignores it.

bytes.description: Size of the photo, at most 6 MiB.

SessionImageChunkRequest.description: One piece of a photo, in order.

SessionImageEndRequest.description: Finishes a photo upload; its path goes to the session with the caption.

CommandsListRequest.description: The slash commands of a session.

PromptAnswerRequest.description: Answers a permission (allow) or a question (choice or text).

choice.description: For a question: a 1-based option number or an option label; an array with one entry per question.

text.description: A free-text answer to a single question, at most 500 characters.

key.description: Additive: one value the phone makes up for each command it sends and repeats unchanged on every retry. A Standby that holds or relays the command uses it to tell a retry of the same command from a different command. Without it, the request id, op and arguments stand in. An older Mac ignores it.

SessionNewRequest.description: Starts a Claude Code session in a folder inside the Mac's home.

modelId.description: A model id from the `models` of sessions.list, such as claude-opus-5-5 (a [1m] or date suffix is accepted). Wins over `model` when both are sent; the Mac answers invalid for an id it doesn't list. An older Mac ignores it.

key.description: Additive: one value the phone makes up for each command it sends and repeats unchanged on every retry. A Standby that holds or relays the command uses it to tell a retry of the same command from a different command. Without it, the request id, op and arguments stand in. An older Mac ignores it.

ChatImageRequest.description: A JPEG of a picture in the chat. The Mac answers with JSON, then a binary IMG1 frame.

SessionTakeoverRequest.description: Resumes a view-only session in a terminal the Mac owns.

stopOriginal.description: Stop the original claude process first.

SubscribeRequest.description: Replaces what the Mac pushes to this connection.

sessions.description: Push the session list and prompts.

sessionId.description: Push new chat messages of this session.

lastMessageId.description: The newest message the phone already has, so the ones after it are pushed.

phone.description: Stream the Mac's device window as PHN1 frames.

inbox.description: Push the inbox's items, and each one raised, changed or removed after. Absent means no inbox pushes.

held.description: Additive: push held.changed when a command held on this Mac is added, delivered, dropped, cancelled or starts waiting. Absent means no held pushes.

InboxAnswerRequest.description: Presses one action of an open inbox item. The first answer wins, from the Mac or a phone.

action.description: An action id the item offers; open is refused.

note.description: A note with the answer, at most 300 characters.

PairResponse.description: Paired: the token is shown once.

models.description: The Claude models a new session may start on now, current ones only, as the Mac's catalog lists them. Absent from an older Mac; the phone then offers its short names.

stale.description: Additive: when the answer comes from a copy that may be behind (a Can Be Master Mac that can't reach the primary), the time of that copy, in milliseconds since 1970. Absent for a live answer.

ChatGetResponse.description: A page of messages, oldest first.

hasMore.description: There are older messages (before) or newer ones (after).

reset.description: The after message is gone; replace what the phone has with this page.

stale.description: Additive: when the answer comes from a copy that may be behind (a Can Be Master Mac that can't reach the primary), the time of that copy, in milliseconds since 1970. Absent for a live answer.

suggested.description: The tab to open first: flow, diagram, entity, chart or web.

WebSnapshotResponse.description: A WEB1 binary frame follows with the same request id; then a second answer, SentResponse.

ChatImageResponse.description: An IMG1 binary frame follows with the same request id; then a second answer, SentResponse.

relayed.description: Additive: true when a Can Be Master Mac that isn't the primary passed the command on to the primary. Absent otherwise.

SessionImageBeginResponse.description: The upload id and the piece size to use.

chunkBytes.description: Send pieces of at most this many bytes.

relayed.description: Additive: true when a Can Be Master Mac that isn't the primary passed the command on to the primary. Absent otherwise.
Additive: true when a Can Be Master Mac that isn't the primary passed the command on to the primary. Absent otherwise.

sessionId.description: The new session's id; a pty: id while it is still starting.

stoppedPid.description: The pid of the original claude process that was stopped.

InboxListResponse.description: The inbox as the Mac keeps it.

InboxAnswerResponse.description: Whether this answer was the one taken.

answered.description: False when the item was already answered, expired or withdrawn.

answer.description: The action that answered the item, when one did.

ErrorResponse.description: The Mac refused a request, or could not read the frame (then there is no id).

message.description: Text for the person, in English. Never parse it.

primary.description: Additive: with primary_unreachable, the name of the primary this Mac couldn't reach.

SessionsEvent.description: The session list changed (also sent once on subscribe).

PromptResolvedEvent.description: A prompt was answered elsewhere or timed out.

ChatEvent.description: New messages in the subscribed session.

OpenEvent.description: The person chose Open on the Mac: the phone should come to the front.

InboxEvent.description: An inbox item was raised or changed. Sent only to a connection that subscribed with inbox: true.

InboxRemovedEvent.description: An inbox item was removed from the Mac's inbox.

ClusterNode.description: Additive: a Can Be Master machine of the Mac's cluster, for a phone that wants a way in when the primary is down.

addrs.description: Addresses the machine's bridge may be reached at, host:port.

fingerprint.description: The SHA-256 fingerprint, lower-case hex, of the certificate this machine's bridge serves.

online.description: False while the Mac answering can't reach it.

HelloCluster.description: Additive: the cluster this Mac belongs to. Absent from a Mac in no cluster and from an older Mac; the phone then knows one machine.

term.description: The primary's term; a higher one is newer.

HeldRef.description: A command this Mac holds until the primary can be reached.

id.description: The held command's id, for held.cancel and held.confirm.

at.description: When it was held, in milliseconds since 1970.

HeldEntry.description: A command held on this Mac, in the order it will be sent.

op.description: The phone op that was held, such as session.message.

sessionId.description: The session it is for, when it is for one.

summary.description: A short line to show, such as the start of the message.

at.description: When it was held, in milliseconds since 1970.

waiting.description: True when it was held for over an hour: it is sent only after held.confirm.

key.description: Additive: the key the phone sent with the command, when it sent one. held.cancel takes it in place of heldId.

HeldNotice.description: A held command that was dropped instead of sent, with the reason to show.

reason.description: Text for the person, in English.

at.description: When it was dropped, in milliseconds since 1970.

HeldListRequest.description: The commands this Mac holds. Paired phone only.

HeldCancelRequest.description: Drops a held command, by heldId or by key. Paired phone only.

heldId.description: The held command's id. Either this or key.

key.description: Additive: the key the phone sent with the command, as an alternative to heldId. Looked up among this phone's own held and sent commands.

HeldConfirmRequest.description: Sends a held command that waited over an hour, after the fresh ones. Paired phone only.

HeldResponse.description: The command is held on this Mac until the primary can be reached; it is not sent yet.

notices.description: The last commands dropped, newest last.

delivered.description: True when the command was already sent, so there was nothing to cancel.

inFlight.description: True when the Mac is sending the command right now and the result isn't known yet, so it can't be cancelled.

HeldConfirmResponse.description: The waiting command will be sent in order.

confirmed.description: False when no waiting command has that id.

HeldChangedEvent.description: What this Mac holds changed. Sent only to a connection that subscribed with held: true.

Request.description: A frame the phone sends; the op says which.

Event.description: A frame the Mac pushes without being asked; the event says which.

ClusterMachine.description: A machine of the cluster, for the phone's Machines popup. Online or not, Can Be Master or not.

canBeMaster.description: False: the machine only controls jobs, it is listed but can't be picked.

ready.description: True when the machine's own readiness checks pass.

setAt.description: Wall time in milliseconds since 1970 of the newest snapshot set the machine holds; absent when it holds none.

canResume.description: canBeMaster, ready and a set: sessions continue there from setAt.

ClusterMachinesRequest.description: Additive: the machines a phone can pick when no primary is reachable. An older Mac answers invalid, and the phone hides the popup. Paired phone only.

ClusterPromoteRequest.description: Additive: move the primary to a machine now, when the old primary can't be reached. Handled on the Mac the phone reached and never held or relayed. Needs the Mac to be allowed to act.

confirmed.description: True after the person saw the text of an earlier needsConfirm answer and chose Move Anyway.

ClusterMachinesResponse.description: The machines of the cluster this Mac knows.

ClusterPromoteResponse.description: What the promote did. One of step, relayed or needsConfirm.

step.description: Where the promote is; it goes on after this answer.

relayed.description: True when the old primary was reachable through another machine: nothing moved.

text.description: With relayed: the words to show, such as m5 is reachable through m1; nothing moved.

needsConfirm.description: The risk the person must accept first; ask again with confirmed true to go on.
